rationale: Measured baseline: median latency_ms 4.2250 with 88 forward CUDA kernels summing to 4152.3 us, i.e. the workload is GPU-bound with only ~73 us host headroom, so host-side plays (graphs, Python trimming) are rejected per the selection evidence. Of that GPU time, 889.7 us (21.4%) is memory-bound eager pointwise work produced by the transformers 5.16.1 structure in the selected region: 20 separate cudnn bn_fw_inf_1C11_kernel_NCHW passes (425.4 us), 17 separate clamp/vectorized ReLU passes (343.9 us) and 8 CUDAFunctor_add passes (120.4 us) (target-resources.json). This candidate replaces exactly the selected region (all 5 groups: ResNetEmbeddings plus the 8 ResNetBasicLayer modules) with a fused pointwise policy that leaves every convolution and the stem max-pool on the parent compute path, invoked directly on the actual nn.Module instances from context['modules'] (Conv2d dispatch, cudnn kernels, numerics and output tensors unchanged): stem conv7x7 -> one Triton kernel computing relu(a*x+b) with a=weight*rsqrt(var+eps), b=bias-mean*a (the same eval-BN affine formula the native inference kernel uses) -> parent MaxPool2d; each block: conv1 -> fused [BN1 affine + ReLU] kernel, conv2 -> fused [BN2 affine + shortcut add + ReLU] kernel reading the residual (identity input or the parent shortcut conv+BN module output, which keeps its native BN). Per block the 5 full-tensor passes (bn1, relu1, bn2, add, relu2) become 2 passes whose elementwise arithmetic association ((x*a)+b)+s matches the parent's sequence; per stem 2 passes become 1. 42 eager pointwise kernel launches (17 main-path BN + 17 ReLU + 8 add) collapse into 17 Triton kernels; tensor traffic for those chains drops from 11 passes/block+stem to 5/2, so at the observed ~0.9-1.4 TB/s effective bandwidth the pointwise pool should shrink from 889.7 us to roughly 380-450 us (the 3 shortcut BNs, ~18 us, stay native), targeting latency_ms 4.225 -> ~3.75-3.9 ms. Numerical risk is ULP-level: conv outputs stay bit-identical, and the fused constants reproduce the native eval-BN affine up to rsqrt/FMA rounding (CPU check: derived a,b reproduce native BN output exactly), far below the 1e-4 logits tolerance; require_exact_top1 flips only if a fixture row's top-2 logit gap were within ~1e-5, which the fused-drift bound makes unlikely but is validated by the framework's paired quality check rather than assumed. No inputs/previous-candidate and no previous-feedback.txt exist, so this is the first attempt on this revision. Peak allocations are unchanged in shape (fused outputs replace equal-sized bn/relu/add intermediates; no new pools beyond ~19 KB of packed BN constants), so the memory goal and the images_per_second>=0.95 baseline ratio are preserved while latency is reduced. Execution requirement note (prose, not a bundle reference): the fused kernels rely on the triton 3.7.1 package that already ships inside the pinned worker environment /root/autodl-tmp/dev-venv (torch 2.13.0+cu129, worker-environment.json); it is an environment property, not an installed candidate bundle, so requires/replaces are empty arrays and any Triton unavailability degrades route-by-route to the parent forward instead of failing.
setup_work: build() runs once at installation before validation. Per physical module (one 'run' phase each; no multi-phase packing to share): structural verification of the actual nn.Module tree (Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU/MaxPool2d/Identity types, eval mode, affine BN present), then one-time packing of eval-BN affine constants a=weight*rsqrt(var+eps), b=bias-mean*a for the 17 fused BNs (stem + 2 per block) as contiguous float32 device tensors computed under torch.no_grad from the live module parameters. Total setup allocation: 34 small tensors, <=512 floats each, ~19 KB device memory, retained for the module lifetime; the checkpoint parameter tensors themselves are never mutated (derived constants only), and nothing fixture-dependent is precomputed. Two Triton JIT kernels (_bn_relu_kernel, _bn_add_relu_kernel, BLOCK=1024, num_warps=4, channel-major grid) compile lazily on first use, which lands in the framework's quality/coverage execution and the 2 warmup calls, ahead of the 5 timed samples; compilation is in-process cached and the timed window then launches only steady-state kernels. No CUDA Graph capture is used, so no retained graph pools are introduced and no invocation-boundary work is moved outside run(). Triton kernel-module loading is driver allocation outside the PyTorch allocator counters; no claim is made about it.
quality_risks: FMA/rounding order differs from the cudnn BN kernel and the separate add kernel by ~1 ULP per element (rsqrt of var+eps, fma(x,a,b) vs fl(fl(x*a)+b), and the (+s) rounding position); expected logits drift is O(1e-6) relative, well under atol/rtol 1e-4, but it is only bounded by the framework's paired logits comparison, not proven here.

require_exact_top1: an argmax flip requires a top-2 logit gap below the fused drift (~1e-5 absolute); unlikely for the three pinned fixture images, but it is a discrete failure mode the exact-top-1 check must confirm on the GPU.

Triton availability/perf: triton 3.7.1 ships with the pinned torch 2.13.0+cu129 worker; if import or first-launch fails at runtime, every replacement falls back to the parent forward via context['references'] with a 'parent_fallback_error'/'setup_fallback_parent' route label, preserving correctness at baseline speed.

First-invocation JIT compile cost (~1-3 s for 2 kernels) must stay inside quality/warmup execution; it is outside the timed samples by the harness boundary but is acknowledged as setup cost the framework observes.

tl.maximum(y, 0.0) maps NaN to 0 like the cudnn relu epilogue rather than propagating NaN like aten relu; only relevant for non-finite inputs, which the pinned finite FP32 fixture and weights do not produce.

Guards (cuda/float32/4D/contiguous/exact channel and z-vs-shortcut shape match) fall back to the parent forward with 'parent_fallback_guard' on any unexpected signature, so no observed-compatible shape is ever computed on an unsupported path; the in-place parent add is replaced by an out-of-place fused write into a fresh tensor, which is alias-equivalent because the parent's += target (the conv2-BN output) is block-local and never aliased elsewhere, and the block input is never mutated by either implementation.
